Agent-based installer configuration

  • The following YAML files - install-config.yaml and agent-config.yaml files are required for agent-installer ISO.

    [root@rb-bastion files]# cat install-config.yaml
    apiVersion: v1
    baseDomain: ocpagp.com
    metadata:
      name: ocp420
    compute:
    - name: worker
      replicas: 2
    controlPlane:
      name: master
      replicas: 3
    networking:
      networkType: OVNKubernetes
      machineNetwork:
      - cidr: 192.168.160.0/24
    platform:
      none: {}
    pullSecret: '<pull_secret>'
    sshKey: |
      <ssh_public_key>
    imageDigestSources:
    - mirrors:
      - rb-bastion.ocpagp.com:8443/openshift/release
      source: quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-v4.0-art-dev
    - mirrors:
      - rb-bastion.ocpagp.com:8443/openshift/release-images
      source: quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-release
    - mirrors:
      - rb-bastion.ocpagp.com:8443/openshift4
      source: registry.redhat.io/openshift4
    - mirrors:
      - rb-bastion.ocpagp.com:8443/migration-toolkit-virtualization
      source: registry.redhat.io/migration-toolkit-virtualization
    - mirrors:
      - rb-bastion.ocpagp.com:8443/container-native-virtualization
      source: registry.redhat.io/container-native-virtualization
    additionalTrustBundle: |
      -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
      <certificate_content>
      -----END CERTIFICATE-----

Conclusion

  • This white paper provides an end‑to‑end description for building and operating Red Hat OpenShift in air-gap environments. It provides step-by-step instructions for cluster setup, private/local registry configuration, and image and operator mirroring. It concludes with clear guidance to implement policy-driven data protection on the same cluster using Dell PPDM with DDVE, including backup and restore workflows for disconnected operations across containers and VM workloads.

    For customers, this validated design reduces deployment risk, standardizes secure operations in regulated or remote sites, and accelerates time‑to‑value. By unifying platform, storage, and data protection, it enables seamless provisioning, persistent storage integration, and reliable, application‑aware backups and restores for business‑critical workloads.

Container Storage Module custom resource

  • The following YAML file is a CSM Custom resource file used for the deployment of CSM.

    [root@rb-bastion csi]# cat powerflex-csm.yaml
    apiVersion: storage.dell.com/v1
    kind: ContainerStorageModule
    metadata:
      name: vxflexos
      namespace: vxflexos
    spec:
      driver:
        csiDriverType: "powerflex"
        authSecret: "vxflexos-config"
        configVersion: "v2.16.1"
        replicas: 1
        csiDriverSpec:
          fSGroupPolicy: "File"
          storageCapacity: true
        common:
          image: rb-bastion.ocpagp.com:8443/dell-csm-operator/csi-vxflexos:v2.16.1
          imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
          envs:
            - name: X_CSI_SDC_ENABLED
              value: "true"
            - name: X_CSI_DEBUG
              value: "true"
            - name: CSI_LOG_LEVEL
              value: "INFO"
            - name: KUBELET_CONFIG_DIR
              value: "/var/lib/kubelet"
        initContainers:
          - name: sdc
            image: rb-bastion.ocpagp.com:8443/dell-csm-operator/sdc:5.0
            imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
        sideCars:
          - name: provisioner
            enabled: true
            image: rb-bastion.ocpagp.com:8443/dell-csm-operator/csi-provisioner:v6.1.0
          - name: attacher
            enabled: true
            image: rb-bastion.ocpagp.com:8443/dell-csm-operator/csi-attacher:v4.10.0
          - name: resizer
            enabled: true
            image: rb-bastion.ocpagp.com:8443/dell-csm-operator/csi-resizer:v2.0.0
          - name: snapshotter
            enabled: true
            image: rb-bastion.ocpagp.com:8443/dell-csm-operator/csi-snapshotter:v8.4.0
          - name: registrar
            enabled: true
            image: rb-bastion.ocpagp.com:8443/dell-csm-operator/csi-node-driver-registrar:v2.15.0
          - name: external-health-monitor
            enabled: false
            image: rb-bastion.ocpagp.com:8443/dell-csm-operator/csi-external-health-monitor-controller:v0.16.0
            args: ["--monitor-interval=60s"]
          - name: sdc-monitor
            enabled: false
            image: rb-bastion.ocpagp.com:8443/dell-csm-operator/sdc:5.0
            envs:
              - name: MDM
                value: "192.168.151.130,192.168.152.130,192.168.153.130,192.168.154.130"
      modules:
        - name: resiliency
          enabled: true
          configVersion: "v1.15.0"
          components:
            - name: podmon-controller
              image: rb-bastion.ocpagp.com:8443/dell-csm-operator/podmon:v1.15.0
              imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
              args:
                - "--labelvalue=csi-vxflexos"
                - "--skipArrayConnectionValidation=false"
                - "--driverPodLabelValue=dell-storage"
                - "--ignoreVolumelessPods=false"
                - "--arrayConnectivityPollRate=5"
                - "--arrayConnectivityConnectionLossThreshold=3"
                - "--csisock=unix:/var/run/csi/csi.sock"
                - "--mode=controller"
                - "--driver-config-params=/vxflexos-config-params/driver-config-params.yaml"
            - name: podmon-node
              image: rb-bastion.ocpagp.com:8443/dell-csm-operator/podmon:v1.15.0
              imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
              envs:
                - name: "X_CSI_PODMON_API_PORT"
                  value: "8083"
              args:
                - "--labelvalue=csi-vxflexos"
                - "--leaderelection=false"
                - "--driverPodLabelValue=dell-storage"
                - "--ignoreVolumelessPods=false"
                - "--arrayConnectivityPollRate=5"
                - "--csisock=unix:/var/lib/kubelet/plugins/vxflexos.emc.dell.com/csi_sock"
                - "--mode=node"
                - "--driver-config-params=/vxflexos-config-params/driver-config-params.yaml"
    [root@rb-bastion csi]#

Data Domain Virtual Edition

  • PowerProtect Data Domain Virtual Edition (DDVE) is a software-defined data protection appliance which provides scalable backup, recovery, and disaster protection. It delivers enterprise-grade capabilities including inline deduplication, compression, encryption, and replication, significantly reducing storage requirements while ensuring data integrity and fast restores. DDVE supports multiple access protocols (NFS, CIFS, DD Boost, and VTL), which integrates with backup applications, and enables efficient data movement through features like Cloud Tier and replication. It also includes strong security (encryption, MFA, retention lock), centralized management through GUI/CLI, and monitoring/analytics tools, making it a flexible and secure solution for modern data protection needs

    Note: For more details on PowerProtect DDVE, see PowerProtect and Data Domain documentation, and for file system installation and configuration, see the Installation guide.

Data protection with PowerProtect Data Manager

  • On Red Hat OpenShift, PPDM delivers Kubernetes‑native protection for both containerized apps and OpenShift Virtualization (KubeVirt) VMs by leveraging OpenShift API for Data Protection (OADP) and the KubeVirt Velero plugin. Administrators define namespace‑scoped policies with precise include/exclude controls to protect PVCs for containers and DataVolumes/VM disks for VMs, then perform targeted restores of specific PVCs, VMs, or disks without reverting entire namespaces. Backup data is written to DDVE (or PowerProtect appliances) for deduplicated, cyber‑resilient retention.

    Note: To deploy PPDM, see Dell PowerProtect Data Manager Deployment Guide.

    Note: To deploy DDVE, see Dell PowerProtect Data Domain Virtual Edition Installation and Administration Guide.

Home > Storage > PowerFlex > White Papers > Red Hat OpenShift in Air-Gap Environments with Dell PowerFlex > Deployment instructions

Deployment instructions

  • Follow the instructions below to complete the offline deployment of PowerFlex CSM/CSI on the OCP cluster:

    1. On the workstation node, create a ImageSetConfiguration that includes only the Dell CSM Operator. A sample configuration file (filename: imageset-operators-dell-csm.yaml) is provided below: 
      apiVersion: mirror.openshift.io/v2alpha1
      kind: ImageSetConfiguration
      mirror:
        operators:
          - catalog: registry.redhat.io/redhat/certified-operator-index:v4.20
            packages:
              - name: dell-csm-operator-certified
                channels:
                  - name: stable
                    minVersion: "v1.11.3"
    2. Download the images on the workstation using the following command: 
      $ oc mirror --v2 --config imageset-operators-dell-csm.yaml file:///data/oc-mirror-dell-csm
    3. Move the entire directory contents from the workstation node to the bastion node using the scp command.
    4. On the bastion node, push the images to the local registry using the following command: 
      $ oc mirror --v2 -c imageset-operators-dell-csm.yaml --from   file:///data/oc-mirror-dell-csm docker://<MIRROR_REGISTRY_HOST>:<PORT>
    5. oc mirror generates manifests that must be applied so that the cluster pulls from the mirror registry and can consume the mirrored catalogs. 
      $ oc apply -f /data/oc-mirror-dell-csm/working-dir/cluster-resources
    6. Install CSM operator by logging into the OpenShift UI -> Ecosystem -> Software Catalog and click Dell Container Storage Modules tile. Click Install to complete the CSM operator deployment.
    7. On the workstation node, create a ImageSetConfiguration file that includes the PowerFlex CSI driver images. A sample configuration file (filename: imageset-dell-csi.yaml) is provided below: 
      apiVersion: mirror.openshift.io/v2alpha1
      kind: ImageSetConfiguration
      mirror:
        additionalImages:
          - name: quay.io/dell/container-storage-modules/csi-vxflexos:v2.16.1
          - name: quay.io/dell/container-storage-modules/podmon:v1.15.0
          - name: quay.io/dell/storage/powerflex/sdc:5.0
          - name: registry.k8s.io/sig-storage/csi-provisioner:v6.1.0
          - name: registry.k8s.io/sig-storage/csi-attacher:v4.10.0
          - name: registry.k8s.io/sig-storage/csi-resizer:v2.0.0
          - name: registry.k8s.io/sig-storage/csi-snapshotter:v8.4.0
          - name: registry.k8s.io/sig-storage/csi-node-driver-registrar:v2.15.0
          - name: registry.k8s.io/sig-storage/csi-external-health-monitor-controller:v0.16.0
    8. Download the images on the workstation using the following command: 
      $ oc mirror --v2 --config imageset-dell-csi.yaml file:///data/oc-mirror-dell-csi
    9. Move the entire directory contents from workstation node to bastion node using the scp command.
    10. On the bastion node, push the images to the local registry using the following command: 
      $ oc mirror -c imageset-dell-csi.yaml  --v2 --from file:///data/oc-mirror-dell-csi docker://<MIRROR_REGISTRY_HOST>:<PORT>
    11. Create ContainerStorageModule CR with the required configuration and apply it to the cluster. A sample CSM CR is provided in the Sample YAML files section.
    12. Verify all the driver pods are running using the following commands: 
      [root@rb-bastion csi]# oc get csm
      NAME       CREATIONTIME   CSIDRIVERTYPE   CONFIGVERSION   VERSION   STATE
      vxflexos   3d2h           powerflex       v2.16.1                   Succeeded

      [root@rb-bastion csi]# oc get pods -n vxflexos
      NAME                                   READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
      vxflexos-controller-5b7cd66565-h7nxt   6/6     Running   0          3d
      vxflexos-node-khpqf                    3/3     Running   0          3d
      vxflexos-node-qjjkk                    3/3     Running   0          3d
      [root@rb-bastion csi]#
      Note: For more information about deployment of Dell CSM on a disconnected OpenShift environment, see Installing Dell CSM Operator on a disconnected OpenShift environment.

    13. Create the storage class for PowerFlex. A sample storageclass YAML file is provided below: 
      apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
      kind: StorageClass
      metadata:
        name: vxflexos-sc
        annotations:
          storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class: "true"
          storageclass.beta.kubernetes.io/is-default-class: "true"
      provisioner: csi-vxflexos.dellemc.com
      parameters:
        storagepool: "SP-1"
        protectiondomain: "PD-1"
        fsType: "xfs"
      reclaimPolicy: Delete
      allowVolumeExpansion: true
      volumeBindingMode: Immediate

      # kubectl apply -f storageclass.yaml
    Note: For more details on the configurable parameters for storage class, see Creating storage classes.

Deployment of PowerFlex CSM and CSI driver

  • This section describes the PowerFlex CSM and CSI driver deployment on the fully disconnected OpenShift cluster. The CSI Driver for PowerFlex is a Container Storage Interface (CSI) driver that provides support for provisioning persistent storage using the Dell PowerFlex storage cluster.

    PowerFlex CSI supports the automatic installation of Software Defined Client (SDC) on compute nodes that are part of OCP cluster. These nodes will use PowerFlex storage to provision persistent volumes.

Executive summary

  • Organizations and enterprises across industries are increasingly adopting Kubernetes platforms like OpenShift Container Platform (OCP) to accelerate digital transformation, modernize applications, and achieve operational consistency across hybrid cloud environments. These container orchestration platforms enable enterprises to deploy and manage applications at scale while ensuring developer productivity and operational efficiency.

    For organizations operating in highly regulated industries, deploying OCP in air-gapped environments helps them meet stringent compliance requirements, protect sensitive intellectual property, and eliminate external attack vectors. These isolated networks ensure complete control over external connectivity but require specialized data protection strategies, which Dell seamlessly addresses.

    Dell PowerFlex is a software-defined infrastructure platform that delivers exceptional performance, scalability, and flexibility for modern workloads. When integrated with OCP through its Container Storage Module (CSM) and CSI driver, PowerFlex provides enterprise-grade storage capabilities, enabling dynamic provisioning, high availability, and seamless data management for containerized applications.

    Building on this storage foundation, the following solution adds data protection with Dell PowerProtect Data Manager (PPDM) and Dell Data Domain Virtual Edition (DDVE). PPDM delivers centralized backup and recovery management for both container and virtual machine workloads using CSI-based, application-consistent snapshots, while DDVE offers efficient deduplication and secure storage capabilities, ensuring reliable disaster recovery.

    This white paper covers the deployment of OCP in air-gapped environments, including the configuration of PowerFlex CSM/CSI for dynamic volume provisioning. It details the deployment architecture of PPDM and DDVE within the air-gapped infrastructure, demonstrating how these components work together to provide enterprise-grade data protection. The document describes use cases for backup and restore operations using PPDM and DDVE, covering both containerized workloads and virtual machines, enabling organizations to implement reliable disaster recovery strategies while maintaining strict security and compliance requirements.

Installation steps

  • The deployment of OpenShift Container Platform (OCP) in a fully disconnected, air-gapped environment can be organized into four distinct phases.

    1. Creation of the local mirror registry on the Bastion host to provide an internal image source for the fully disconnected environment.
    2. Execution of the fully disconnected mirroring workflow for OCP release images and required operators by using oc mirror --v2 in a Mirror-to-Disk and Disk-to-Mirror sequence.
    3. Installation of the OpenShift cluster on bare metal servers by using the Agent-based Installer.
    4. Post-install configuration of the cluster by applying the oc mirror --v2 generated resources—such as IDMS, ITMS, and catalog resources—so that the cluster continuously consumes images from the local mirror registry.
    • Local mirror registry on the bastion host
    • Mirroring images for a disconnected installation
    • Installing OCP cluster with the agent-based Installer
    • Post-install configuration of the cluster

Installation steps

  • Local mirror registry on the bastion host

    A fully disconnected OCP deployment requires a locally hosted mirror registry within the isolated environment so that the cluster can retrieve platform images and operator content without access to external registries. In this solution, the local mirror registry is deployed on the bastion host and serves as the persistent internal image source for the disconnected OpenShift deployment.


    Prerequisites

    The following prerequisites must be met before installing the mirror registry on the bastion host:

    • A supported operating system is available on the bastion host, typically RHEL 8.x or RHEL 9.x.
    • Required host utilities, including Podman and OpenSSL, are installed.
    • A resolvable fully qualified domain name (FQDN) is configured for the registry endpoint (FQDN:Port_number). In this solution, the endpoint is rb-bastion.ocpagp.com:8443.
    • Mirror registry bundle (mirror-registry-amd64.tar.gz) must be available on the bastion host. This tool must be downloaded on the workstation host from OpenShift console Downloads page and then securely transferred to the bastion host.

    Deployment procedure

    Install the mirror registry from the mirror-registry-amd64.tar.gz bundle on the bastion host. The following commands extract the installer archive, changes into the extracted directory, and launches the registry installation with the Quay hostname, administrative user, and storage location specified.

    $ mkdir -p ~/mirror-registry

    $ tar -xvzf mirror-registry-amd64.tar.gz -C ~/mirror-registry

    $ cd ~/mirror-registry

    $ ./mirror-registry install \
      --quayHostname rb-bastion.ocpagp.com \
      --initUser admin \
      --initPassword '<secure-password>' \
      --quayStorage /opt/quay-storage

    For more information, see Creating a mirror registry with mirror registry for Red Hat OpenShift.

    Note: OpenShift mirror registry is not a highly available, enterprise-grade registry, and it is only supported for hosting images required for cluster deployment. Post-installation, the customer should use an enterprise-grade registry. For more details, see Mirror registry for Red Hat OpenShift limitations.

Installation steps

  • Mirroring images for a disconnected installation

    For the disconnected installation of OCP cluster, install the cluster by using the mirrored OCP images available in a private registry.

    The oc-mirror plugin v2 tool mirrors images to a mirror registry in a fully or partially disconnected environment. The mirroring of images consists of the following steps:

    • On the workstation host, create an image set configuration file to pull OCP images.
    • On the workstation host, mirror an image set to disk (mirror to disk, resulting in tar file), transfer the tar file to the bastion host, then mirror the image set to the mirror registry (disk to mirror) on the bastion host.
    • Configure the cluster to use the resources generated by the oc-mirror plugin v2.

    Prerequisites

    • Download the oc-mirror CLI plugin from the Downloads page of the Red Hat Hybrid Cloud Console and install it. For more information, see Installing the oc-mirror OpenShift CLI plugin.
    • Create container image registry credentials file to mirror images from Red Hat to the local mirror using the instructions below:
      • Download pull secret from Red Hat OpenShift Cluster Manager. This pull secret contains the credentials to access registry.redhat.io..
      • Create a JSON format of the pull secret by following the command below:
        $ cat ./pull-secret | jq . > <path>/<pull_secret_file_in_json>
      • If the $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/containers directory does not exist, create one by entering the following command:
        $ mkdir -p $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/containers
      • Save the pull secret file as $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/containers/auth.json.
      • Generate the base64-encoded username and password to access the local mirror registry by running the following command:
        $ echo -n '<user_name>:<password>' | base64 -w0
      • Edit $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/containers/auth.json file and add a section that describes the local mirror registry, a sample section is provided below:
        "auths": {
            "rb-bastion.ocpagp.com:8443": {
              "auth": "<base64_encoded_credentals>"
            }
          }

    For more information, see Configuring credentials that allow images to be mirrored.


    Define the ImageSetConfiguration

    Create an ImageSetConfiguration file specifying the OCP version, any operators to be included, and so on. The sample file (filename: imageset-config-ocp42019-virt-nmstate.yaml) below shows the configuration for installing OCP 4.20.x, Red Hat Operator Index v4.20 catalog, kubevirt-hyperconverged operator package and the kubernetes-nmstate-operator package.

    apiVersion: mirror.openshift.io/v2alpha1
    kind: ImageSetConfiguration
    mirror:
      platform:
        channels:
          - name: stable-4.20
            type: ocp
      operators:
        - catalog: registry.redhat.io/redhat/redhat-operator-index:v4.20
          packages:
            - name: kubevirt-hyperconverged
              channels:
                - name: stable
            - name: kubernetes-nmstate-operator
              channels:
                - name: stable

    Mirror the image set to disk (mirror-to-disk)

    The following command creates an archive directory and uses oc mirror tool to mirror the image set to the archive directory.

    $ export OCM_ARCHIVE_DIR=/opt/oc-mirror/ocp42019-virt-nmstate
    $ mkdir -p "${OCM_ARCHIVE_DIR}"
    $ oc mirror -c imageset-config-ocp42019-virt-nmstate.yaml \
      file://${OCM_ARCHIVE_DIR} \
      --v2

    When the mirror-to-disk stage completes successfully, the archive directory contains:

    • One or more tar archives containing the mirrored image content.
    • A working-dir/cluster-resources directory containing generated manifests that will be required later to configure the cluster to consume the local mirror registry.

    Transfer the archive set into the disconnected environment

    After the mirror-to-disk stage is completed, transfer the entire archive directory along with the ImageSetConfiguration file and the $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/containers/auth.json into the disconnected environment (bastion host) by using an approved secure transfer mechanism (removable media or scp).

    Note: In the lab environment, SCP was used to transfer the contents from workstation host to the bastion host.

    The transfer must preserve both the image archives and the generated working-dir content, because the latter contains cluster resource manifests that are required later for post-install configuration.

    Disk-to-mirror into the local registry

    Import the archived content into the bastion-hosted registry at rb-bastion.ocpagp.com:8443 using the following commands:

    $ export OCM_ARCHIVE_DIR=/opt/oc-mirror/ocp42019-virt-nmstate

    $ oc mirror -c imageset-config-ocp42019-virt-nmstate.yaml \
      --from file://${OCM_ARCHIVE_DIR} \
      docker://rb-bastion.ocpagp.com:8443 \
      --v2
    ...
    ....
    2026/04/30 14:23:38  [INFO]   : === Results ===
    2026/04/30 14:23:38  [INFO]   :  âœ“  193 / 193 release images mirrored successfully
    2026/04/30 14:23:38  [INFO]   :  âœ“  66 / 66 operator images mirrored successfully
    2026/04/30 14:23:38  [INFO]   : ðŸ“„ Generating IDMS file...
    2026/04/30 14:23:38  [INFO]   : /opt/oc-mirror/ocp42019-virt-nmstate/working-dir/cluster-resources/idms-oc-mirror.yaml file created
    2026/04/30 14:23:38  [INFO]   : ðŸ“„ Generating ITMS file...
    2026/04/30 14:23:38  [INFO]   : /opt/oc-mirror/ocp42019-virt-nmstate/working-dir/cluster-resources/itms-oc-mirror.yaml file created
    2026/04/30 14:23:38  [INFO]   : ðŸ“„ Generating CatalogSource file...
    2026/04/30 14:23:38  [INFO]   : /opt/oc-mirror/ocp42019-virt-nmstate/cluster-resources/cs-redhat-operator-index-v4-20.yaml file created
    2026/04/30 14:23:38  [INFO]   : ðŸ“„ Generating ClusterCatalog file...
    2026/04/30 14:23:38  [INFO]   : /opt/oc-mirror/ocp42019-virt-nmstate/working-dir/cluster-resources/cc-redhat-operator-index-v4-20.yaml file created
    2026/04/30 14:23:38  [INFO]   : ðŸ“„ Generating Signature Configmap...
    2026/04/30 14:23:38  [INFO]   : /opt/oc-mirror/ocp42019-virt-nmstate/working-dir/cluster-resources/signature-configmap.json file created
    2026/04/30 14:23:38  [INFO]   : /opt/oc-mirror/ocp42019-virt-nmstate/working-dir/cluster-resources/signature-configmap.yaml file created
    2026/04/30 14:23:38  [INFO]   : mirror time     : 26m56.076777226s
    2026/04/30 14:23:38  [INFO]   : ðŸ‘‹ Goodbye, thank you for using oc-mirror

    This disk-to-mirror stage pushes the mirrored OCP release payload and operator content into the local registry so that the disconnected cluster can consume them.

Home > Storage > PowerFlex > White Papers > Red Hat OpenShift in Air-Gap Environments with Dell PowerFlex > Installation steps

Installation steps

  • Installing OCP cluster with the agent-based Installer


    Prerequisites

    • Download the below utilities from Red Hat Hybrid Cloud Console using Red Hat login credentials to the workstation node. After downloading, move these utilities to bastion node.
      • openshift-install
      • oc client
      • oc-mirror plugin
      • pull secret

    For more information, see Downloading the Agent-based Installer.

    Note: Make sure to download the same version of the utilities as the OCP version being installed.

    • Container image registry credentials file.
    • SSH public key of the bastion node for cluster node access.

    Deployment procedure

    Deployment of an OCP cluster in an air-gap environment using the agent-based installer requires an agent-based installer ISO. Follow the instructions below for creating the ISO and using it for deployment.

    1. Create two configuration files:
      • install-config.yaml - This file defines the overall OpenShift cluster configuration that the installer uses to build and install the cluster. This file includes the information below:
        • Cluster identity: metadata.name, baseDomain
        • Platform: baremetal, none, external, or vSphere
        • Node topology: control plane and worker replica counts
        • Networking: machine network, cluster network, service network, VIPs
        • Access/authentication: pullSecret, sshKey
        • Optional install-time settings such as trust bundles, FIPS, mirroring, and capabilities
      • agent-config.yaml - This file defines the agent-specific host and node details that the agent-based installer needs to discover machines and drive installation. This file includes the information below:
        • Rendezvous host IP (rendezvousIP) - the node that initially runs the Assisted Service/bootstrap workflow
        • Host inventory - each machine's hostname and role (master / worker)
        • Interface MAC addresses for matching discovered hosts
        • Per-host network configurations such as static IPs, bonds, VLANs, routes, DNS, and NTP sources
        • Optional root device hints and other node-specific settings.

      For more information about the options configured in install-config.yaml and agent-config.yaml,see Installing a cluster with customizations.

      A sample install-config.yaml and agent-config.yaml are provided in Sample YAML files.

    2. Generate the agent-installer ISO using the following command: 
      $ openshift-install --dir <INSTALL_DIRECTORY> agent create image

      INSTALL_DIRECTORY is a directory which consists of the install-config.yaml and agent-config.yaml files.

    3. To create OCP cluster with 3 control plane nodes and 2 worker nodes, boot control plane node-1 (also called as rendezvous host or bootstrap host) with the agent ISO.
    4. In the Rendezvous node setup page, select This is the rendezvous node.
    5. In the Rendezvous node IP selection screen, select the IP address in the disconnected network environment.
    6. A confirmation message is displayed after successfully configuring the rendezvous node IP. Click Continue.
    7. The server will complete the booting process. Wait for ~10 minutes for the assisted service to start on this server and the IP address to display to access the assisted installer.
    8. Connect to the IP address from a browser. In the Cluster details page, update Cluster name, base domain, paste the pull secret and choose the number of control plane nodes and click Next.
    9. In the Operators screen, select any additional operators to install and click Next.
    10. In the Host discovery screen, the assisted installer automatically discovers the bootstrap node.
    11. Map the agent ISO to the other cluster nodes and boot them from the ISO image.
    12. In the Rendezvous node setup screen, provide the IP of the Rendezvous node and click on Save rendezvous IP.
    13. In the confirmation screen, click Continue. The hosts will complete the boot process.
    14. The Host discovery screen detects and displays all OCP nodes. Update the Roles for all the nodes.
    15. On the Storage page, verify the correct disks on the OCP nodes are selected for OS installation. Click Next.
    16. On the Networking page, update the API IP and Ingress IP field. Enter the SSH public key of the bastion node in Host SSH Public Key for troubleshooting after installation field. Click Next.
    17. In the Download credentials page, select the checkbox to acknowledge that to download credential files prior to cluster installation. Click Download credentials and save the cluster credentials file in a secure location.
    18. In the Review and create page, review all the cluster details and click Install cluster to start the cluster installation.
    19. Monitor the bootstrap process using the following command: 
      openshift-install --dir <INSTALL_DIRECTORY> agent wait-for bootstrap-complete --log-level=info
      ..................................................................
      ..................................................................
      INFO Bootstrap configMap status is complete
      INFO cluster bootstrap is complete
    20. Monitor the cluster installation process using the following command: 
      openshift-install --dir <INSTALL_DIRECTORY> agent wait-for install-complete
      ..................................................................
      ..................................................................
      INFO Cluster is installed
      INFO Install complete!

Installation steps

  • Post-install configuration of the cluster

    1. Configure the OCP cluster to use the resources generated by oc-mirror plugin by running the following command: 
      $ oc apply -f <path_to_oc_mirror_workspace>/working-dir/cluster-resources
    2. If release images are mirrored, then apply the release image signatures to the cluster by running the following command: 
      $ oc apply -f working-dir/cluster-resources/signature-configmap.json
    3. Verify that the ImageDigestMirrorSet resources are successfully installed by running the following command: 
      $ oc get imagedigestmirrorset
    4. Verify that the ImageTagMirrorSet resources are successfully installed by running the following command: 
      $ oc get imagetagmirrorset
    5. Verify that the CatalogSource resources are successfully installed by running the following command: 
      $ oc get catalogsource -n
                      openshift-marketplace
    6. Verify that the ClusterCatalog resources are successfully installed by running the following command: 
      $ oc get clustercatalog
    7. Install the OpenShift Virtualization and Kubernetes NMState Operators by logging into the OpenShift UI -> Ecosystem -> Software Catalog
    8. Configure the additional networks that are required on the OpenShift nodes to be able to connect to the PowerFlex cluster. The network configuration of the OpenShift nodes, for example, adding or removing network interfaces is configured by applying a NodeNetworkConfigurationPolicy (NNCP) manifest to the cluster. For more information, see Kubernete NMState.

Integrating PPDM with OCP in air-gap environments

  • Mirror all PPDM and DDVE images to a private registry, allowing protection workflows to run fully within air‑gapped environments, covering both containerized applications and VMs using OpenShift Virtualization.

    Follow the instructions below to integrate PPDM with OCP in an air-gap environment:

    1. Create the ImageSetConfiguration that mirrors the OADP operator and the required PPDM/K8s images: 
      # imageset-ppdm-config.yaml
      apiVersion: mirror.openshift.io/v2alpha1
      kind: ImageSetConfiguration
      mirror:
        operators:
          - catalog: registry.redhat.io/redhat/redhat-operator-index:v4.20
            packages:
              - name: redhat-oadp-operator
                channels:
                  - name: stable
        additionalImages:
          - name: docker.io/dellemc/powerprotect-k8s-controller:20.1.0.0-17
          - name: docker.io/dellemc/powerprotect-cproxy:20.1.0.0-17
          - name: docker.io/dellemc/powerprotect-velero-dd:20.1.0.0-17
          - name: docker.io/velero/velero:v1.14.1
          - name: quay.io/konveyor/openshift-velero-plugin:release-1.4.4
          - name: docker.io/vsphereveleroplugin/velero-plugin-for-vsphere:v1.5.4
    2. On the workstation node, download the PPDM images using the following command: 
      $ oc mirror --v2 --config imageset-ppdm-config.yaml file:///data/oc-mirror-dell-ppdm
    3. Move the entire directory contents from workstation node to bastion node using the scp command.
    4. On the bastion node, publish images to local registry and create mirrored catalog by running the following command: 
      $ export REG_MIRROR=rb-bastion.ocpagp.com:8443
      $ podman login $REG_MIRROR
      $ oc mirror --v2 -c imageset-ppdm-config.yaml --from file:///data/oc-mirror-dell-ppdm docker://$REG_MIRROR
      $ oc apply -f /data/oc-mirror-dell-ppdm/working-dir/cluster-resources
      $ oc -n openshift-marketplace get catalogsource
    5. Create a new namespace called velero-ppdm.
    6. Install OADP operator by logging into the OpenShift UI -> Ecosystem -> Software Catalog and click OADP Operator. Click Install to complete the installation of OADP operator in the velero-ppdm namespace.
    7. Register the OCP cluster with PPDM: In PPDM UI, to discover and add the OCP cluster, see Enabling the Kubernetes cluster section in Dell PowerProtect Data Manager Kubernetes User Guide.

Home > Storage > PowerFlex > White Papers > Red Hat OpenShift in Air-Gap Environments with Dell PowerFlex > Logical architecture

Logical architecture

  • The following diagram shows the logical architecture of this solution.

    In this solution, for the air-gap environment, a workstation node is used as the Internet-connected preparation host for obtaining tools and building mirror archives and a bastion node is used to host the local container registry for OCP images (private mirror registry). The bastion node also serves as the DNS and DHCP server for the OCP cluster.

    Note: Workstation and bastion node can either be a bare metal server or a virtual machine.

    PowerFlex Manager deploys a PowerFlex storage-only (SO) cluster on five bare metal servers.

    A single PowerFlex protection domain and a single storage pool are configured on PowerFlex. The PowerFlex storage pool topology consists of five PDSs with 10 SSD disks in each of the five PDS nodes.

    An OpenShift cluster with three control plane nodes and two worker nodes is deployed in an air-gap environment. After the cluster deployment, the required PowerFlex data networks are configured on these OpenShift nodes.

    Next, the PowerFlex CSI driver is installed. The PowerFlex Storage Data Client (SDC) is automatically installed by the CSI driver install on the OpenShift worker nodes. The CSI driver for PowerFlex provides support for provisioning persistent storage using the PowerFlex storage cluster. For more information, see Installing the CSI Driver for PowerFlex.

    Finally, PPDM and DDVE are deployed and integrated with OCP to deliver enterprise-grade resilience and disaster recovery.

Network architecture

  • The following figure shows the network architecture of this solution:

    Each PowerFlex SO node is connected to the TOR switches. All nodes are equipped with dual-port NICs, and these network ports are trunked with the TOR switches. The NICs handle management, data1, data2, data3, and data4 network traffic for PowerFlex. The management network operates in active-backup (mode1) bonding. The solution provides dedicated networks for PowerFlex data transfer.

    The solution uses dedicated VLANs to separate management and data network traffic. The following table shows the different VLANs used for PowerFlex SO nodes.

    Table 3. Network VLAN details of PowerFlex SO nodes
    Network type VLAN
    PowerFlex Management 150
    PowerFlex Data 1 151
    PowerFlex Data 2 152
    PowerFlex Data 3 153
    PowerFlex Data 4 154

    The following table shows the different VLAN that are used on compute nodes.

    Table 4. Network VLAN details of PowerFlex compute nodes
    Network type VLAN
    Ingress/API 160
    PowerFlex Data 1 151
    PowerFlex Data 2 152
    PowerFlex Data 3 153
    PowerFlex Data 4 154

PostgreSQL deployment manifest

  • The following YAML file provides PostgreSQL deployment manifest definitions.

    [root@rb-bastion postgres-pod]# cat postgres-deployment.yaml
    apiVersion: v1
    kind: Namespace
    metadata:
      name: postgres
    ---
    apiVersion: v1
    kind: Secret
    metadata:
      name: postgres-secret
      namespace: postgres
    type: Opaque
    data:
      POSTGRESQL_USER: cG9zdGdyZXM=
      POSTGRESQL_PASSWORD: cG9zdGdyZXNwYXNzd29yZA==
      POSTGRESQL_DATABASE: cG9zdGdyZXM=
    ---
    apiVersion: v1
    kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
    metadata:
      name: postgres-pvc
      namespace: postgres
    spec:
      accessModes:
        - ReadWriteOnce
      storageClassName: vxflexos-rb-sp-1
      resources:
        requests:
          storage: 10Gi
    ---
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    metadata:
      name: postgres
      namespace: postgres
    spec:
      replicas: 1
      selector:
        matchLabels:
          app: postgres
      strategy:
        type: Recreate
      template:
        metadata:
          labels:
            app: postgres
        spec:
          securityContext:
            seccompProfile:
              type: RuntimeDefault
          containers:
            - name: postgres
              image: rb-bastion.ocpagp.com:8443/rhel9/postgresql-16:latest
              imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
              securityContext:
                allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
                runAsNonRoot: true
                capabilities:
                  drop:
                    - ALL
              ports:
                - containerPort: 5432
              env:
                - name: POSTGRESQL_USER
                  valueFrom:
                    secretKeyRef:
                      name: postgres-secret
                      key: POSTGRESQL_USER
                - name: POSTGRESQL_PASSWORD
                  valueFrom:
                    secretKeyRef:
                      name: postgres-secret
                      key: POSTGRESQL_PASSWORD
                - name: POSTGRESQL_DATABASE
                  valueFrom:
                    secretKeyRef:
                      name: postgres-secret
                      key: POSTGRESQL_DATABASE
                - name: PGDATA
                  value: /var/lib/pgsql/data
              volumeMounts:
                - name: postgres-storage
                  mountPath: /var/lib/pgsql/data
              livenessProbe:
                exec:
                  command:
                    - pg_isready
                initialDelaySeconds: 30
                periodSeconds: 10
              readinessProbe:
                exec:
                  command:
                    - pg_isready
                initialDelaySeconds: 5
                periodSeconds: 5
              resources:
                requests:
                  memory: "256Mi"
                  cpu: "250m"
                limits:
                  memory: "1Gi"
                  cpu: "1000m"
          volumes:
            - name: postgres-storage
              persistentVolumeClaim:
                claimName: postgres-pvc
    ---
    apiVersion: v1
    kind: Service
    metadata:
      name: postgres-service
      namespace: postgres
    spec:
      selector:
        app: postgres
      ports:
        - port: 5432
          targetPort: 5432
      type: ClusterIP
    [root@rb-bastion postgres-pod]#

PowerFlex CSI/CSM

  • An important component outside of PowerFlex that enables a flexible consumption model for Kubernetes is the PowerFlex CSI driver, developed as a part of the Dell Kubernetes strategy. After loading the CSI driver for PowerFlex into Kubernetes, it can be used to provision persistent volumes from the underlying PowerFlex storage resource. If the Kubernetes deployment is running low on PowerFlex storage resources, you can add PowerFlex storage nodes to increase the system capacity and performance.

    The CSI driver connects the PowerFlex system and Kubernetes deployments. It is a storage broker which dynamically provisions volumes from PowerFlex through the PowerFlex API gateway to the Kubernetes cluster. Once the volume is available on PowerFlex, it is mapped to the requesting pod. If a pod is destroyed or rescheduled, the CSI plug-in ensures that the volumes are remapped upon rescheduling of that pod. 

    • Customers running Kubernetes clusters on PowerFlex use the Dell Container Storage Modules (CSM), which extend the CSI driver capabilities. These modules:
    • Provide enterprise storage capabilities to Kubernetes for cloud-native stateful applications.
    • Reduce management complexity, so that developers can independently use enterprise storage with ease and automate daily operations.
    • Extends storage functionality and capabilities beyond using the CSI driver alone.

    These modules include replication, observability, authorization, application mobility, and resiliency.

    PowerFlex supports multiple operating systems. PowerFlex is validated with the leading Kubernetes distributions as shown in the following figure:

PowerFlex deployment architectures

  • Independent architecture

    In an independent, or disaggregated, architecture some nodes provide storage capacity for data in applications, while other separate and independent nodes provide compute resources for applications and workloads. Compute and storage resources can be scaled independently by adding nodes to the cluster while it remains active. This separation of compute and storage resources helps to minimize software licensing costs in certain situations. This architecture is ideal for high-performance databases and application workloads.

    Disaggregation gives organizations the freedom to choose different LCM options that best align with their operational models. Not only can PowerFlex Manager manage the LCM of PowerFlex storage infrastructure, it can also manage LCM of PowerFlex compute nodes. With this freedom, there is also the choice to manage compute estates that connect to PowerFlex with other tooling.

Home > Storage > PowerFlex > White Papers > Red Hat OpenShift in Air-Gap Environments with Dell PowerFlex > PowerProtect Data Manager

PowerProtect Data Manager

  • Dell PowerProtect Data Manager (PPDM) centralizes policy‑driven, application‑consistent backup and recovery for VMs, databases, files, and Kubernetes across on‑prem and cloud, with automation, self‑service, and RBAC from a single UI/API.

    PPDM can protect Kubernetes workloads and ensure that the data is recoverable. PPDM can be deployed using an Open Virtualization Appliance (OVA) or a machine image and is integrated with PowerProtect DD series appliances as protection storage for backups. PowerProtect Data Manager can be integrated with OpenShift cluster through Kubernetes APIs to discover protectable resotources such as VMs, data volumes and PVCs.

    PowerProtect Data Manager protects two types of Kubernetes cluster assets: Namespaces and PersistentVolumeClaims (PVCs). Data Manager discovers the Kubernetes clusters using the IP address or Fully Qualified Domain Name (FQDN).

    During the discovery process, Data Manager creates the following namespaces in the cluster:

    • Velero-ppdm: This namespace contains a Velero pod to back up metadata to target storage.
    • PowerProtect: This namespace contains a PowerProtect controller pod to drive persistent volume claim snapshots and backups. It sends the backups to the target storage using dynamically deployed cProxy pods.
    Note: For more information, see the PowerProtect Data Manager Kubernetes User Guide.

Prerequisites

  • The deployment of Red Hat OpenShift in an air‑gapped environment requires two utility hosts: a Workstation node and a Bastion node.

    • Workstation node (Internet-connected preparation host): This node must have Internet access and SSH connectivity to the bastion node. This node must also be configured with sufficient local storage (atleast 500 GB) to stage release payloads and Operator catalogs and all the required tools like oc/openshift-install and a mirroring tool (for example oc-mirror with Podman/Skopeo) must be downloaded on this node. On the workstation node, download the Red Hat pull secret which will be used to mirror required images, then transfer the tools, secrets, archives and manifests to the bastion node using secure transfer mechanism (like removable media or scp).
    • Bastion node (lab-only services host): This node is connected only to the lab network. It must be configured with services like DNS server for the cluster domain, DHCP server (to provide DHCP IPs or static IPs) and NTP server. The bastion node must also be configured with a private container registry with trusted TLS and adequate capacity to store mirrored OCP releases, Operator catalogs and any add-on images. All OCP nodes must resolve and reach this registry by FQDN.
    • DNS: Records for ingress and API Virtual IP addresses are required for accessing the cluster. A DNS server is configured on the bastion node.
    • SSH public key: Generate this key on the bastion from where the nodes will be accessed. This key authenticates SSH access to the nodes, for troubleshooting during deployment or for maintenance post-deployment. For more information, see Generating a key pair for cluster node SSH access.
    • NTP server: NTP service is required for time synchronization among hosts. NTP server is configured on the bastion node.

Protection policy for protecting the namespaces and PVCs

  • Protection policies define a set of objectives that apply to specific periods of time. These objectives drive configuration, active protection, and copy-data-management operations that satisfy the business requirements for the specified data. Each plan type has its own set of user objectives. Users with the system admin role can create protection policies.

    Note: In this paper, namespaces ppdm-demo and ppdm-restore are created to demonstrate the backup and restore use-cases.

    PowerProtect Data Manager provides the following options when creating a Kubernetes cluster protection policy:

    • Crash Consistent: Select this type for point-in-time backup of namespaces.
    • Exclusion: Select this type if there are assets within the protection policy that should be excluded from data protection operations.

    Perform the following steps to create a protection policy:

    1. Go to Dashboard > Protection > Protection Policies > Add.
    2. Specify the name for protection policy followed by description and select type as Kubernetes.
    3. Select the purpose of the policy as either crash consistent or exclusion.
    4. Proceed to add the assets for the policy.
    5. Add the objectives and create a backup configuration.
    6. Add the primary backup by specifying the details. In this case, the policy is creating a full backup of the namespace every 1 hour that is retained for 15 days and the backup occurs between 8PM and 6AM IST.
      Note: The DDVE backup is configured as a storage target in PPDM and is used to store backups created through Protection Policies.

    7. A confirmation message indicates that Protection Policy for the asset is created.
    8. The Protection policy will be listed in the Policies section as shown below.

Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform

  • Red Hat OpenShift is an enterprise-grade Kubernetes platform that enables organizations to build, deploy, and manage applications at scale across hybrid cloud environments. Built on open-source Kubernetes, OpenShift provides enhanced security, automated operations, and developer self-service capabilities, making it the strategic choice for mission-critical workloads. A key capability of OpenShift is its versatility in supporting both containerized workloads through native Kubernetes orchestration and virtualized workloads through OpenShift Virtualization, which enables organizations to run traditional virtual machines alongside modern containerized applications on the same platform. This unified approach simplifies infrastructure management, accelerates application modernization initiatives, and provides flexibility for organizations transitioning from virtualization to cloud-native architectures.

    Key features

    • Integrated Image Registry: Provides a built-in, secure container registry for storing and managing container images within the platform.
    • Built-in Monitoring and Logging: Offers comprehensive observability through Prometheus for metrics monitoring and Elasticsearch/Fluentd for log aggregation.
    • Automated Scaling: Enables horizontal pod autoscaling and cluster autoscaling to dynamically adjust resources based on workload demands.
    • Multi-Cluster Management: Delivers centralized control and governance across multiple OpenShift clusters through OpenShift Cluster Manager.
    • Role-Based Access Control (RBAC): Implements granular security policies to manage user permissions and access to platform resources.
    • Operator Framework: Provides automated lifecycle management for applications and infrastructure components through Kubernetes operators.

    OpenShift supports three network connectivity modes for installation and operation.

    • The standard connected mode requires full internet access to pull container images, access Red Hat repositories, and enable automated updates.
    • The disconnected or restricted mode provides partial internet connectivity, where certain components may access external sources while maintaining controlled network policies.
    • The air-gapped mode operates with no internet connectivity, requiring all images, packages, and dependencies to be pre-staged locally through mirrored registries and internal repositories.

    This white paper describes the architecture and implementation details for deploying OpenShift in air-gapped environments, providing practical guidance for organizations requiring isolated infrastructure configurations with complete control over data ingress and egress.

    For more information, see OpenShift Container Platform documentation.

Use case 1: Backup of VM namespace

  • A RHEL 9.6 VM is deployed in the ppdm-demo namespace. PostgreSQL-16 is installed on this VM.

    Note: For more information about VM creation, see Creating a virtual machine and for more information about installing PostgreSQL on RHEL 9, see Installing PostgreSQL.

    Manually trigger the backup of the VM namespace, by performing the following steps:

    1. Before taking a backup, record the status of the Postgres database running in the VM. 
      [root@rhel9-postgress-orig ~]# su - postgres
      [postgres@rhel9-postgress-orig ~]$ psql
      psql (16.8)
      Type "help" for help.
                            ^
      postgres=# \c employees_db ;
      You are now connected to database "employees_db" as user "postgres".
      employees_db=# select * from hr.employees ;
       employee_id | employee_name
      -------------+---------------
           1112001 | Abhiram
           1112002 | Rajneesh
           1112003 | Deepa
           1112004 | Karthick
           1112005 | Hansika
           1112006 | Veer
           1112007 | Shaurya
           1112008 | Shanvi
           1112009 | Balbir
           1112010 | Tejas
      (10 rows)
    2. In PPDM UI, go to Dashboard > Protection > Protection Policies. Select the protection policy and click on Protect Now.
    3. PPDM creates a job with a unique ID and can be seen from Dashboard > Jobs tab.
    4. The status of the job can be observed by clicking on the Job Group ID and then looking in the step log tab.
    5. After the backup is completed, insert a few more records into the Postgres database. 
      employees_db=# select * from hr.employees ;
       employee_id | employee_name
      -------------+---------------
           1112001 | Abhiram
           1112002 | Rajneesh
           1112003 | Deepa
           1112004 | Karthick
           1112005 | Hansika
           1112006 | Veer
           1112007 | Shaurya
           1112008 | Shanvi
           1112009 | Balbir

           1112201 | Ram
           1112202 | Rajiv
           1112203 | Deepak
           1112204 | Tilak
           1112205 | Harpal
      (15 rows)

Use case 2: Restore of VM to same namespace

  • To restore the VM in the same namespace, the following steps are followed:

    Note: Before initiating the restore operation on the same namespace, ensure that the VM is powered off and its associated volumes are removed.

    1. In PPDM UI, go to Dashboard > Restore > Assets and select the asset to be restored and choose Restore.
    2. Select the copy of the backup to be restored. By default, the last successful backup copy is displayed. However, the copy of the backup can be selected from the list from the Change Copy option.
    3. Select the cluster to which the backup would be restored. In this case, the backup is restored to the Original Cluster.
    4. Choose the purpose. In this case, Restore Kubernetes Virtual Machines is selected which will restore the VM and its associated PVCs.
    5. Choose the target namespace for the restore operation, in this case Restore to Original Namespace option is selected.
    6. Select whether the PVCs content needs to be overwritten or skip restore of existing PVC.
    7. In the Options page, choose the different VM behavior options when the restore completes.
    8. Verify the Summary and select Restore.
    9. PPDM creates a unique Job ID, and the status of the job can be viewed from the Dashboard > Jobs tab.
    10. PPDM completes the restore job in the same namespace. To verify the restore, go to the OpenShift UI and power on the VM and login to the Postgres database and verify the records. 
      [root@rhel9-postgress-orig ~]# su - postgres
      [postgres@rhel9-postgress-orig ~]$ psql
      psql (16.8)
      Type "help" for help.

      postgres=# \c employees_db ;
      You are now connected to database "employees_db" as user "postgres".
      employees_db=# select * from hr.employees ;
       employee_id | employee_name
      -------------+---------------
           1112001 | Abhiram
           1112002 | Rajneesh
           1112003 | Deepa
           1112004 | Karthick
           1112005 | Hansika
           1112006 | Veer
           1112007 | Shaurya
           1112008 | Shanvi
           1112009 | Balbir
           1112010 | Tejas
      (10 rows)

      The restore operation returns the Postgres database to the state captured in the backup.

Use case 3: Restore of VM to new namespace

  • Note: For restoring a VM to a new namespace, the KubeVirt velero plugin must be v0.9.0 or above.

    To restore the VM in the new namespace, the steps 1 to 4 are the same as described in the previous use case 2.

    1. In PPDM UI, go to Dashboard > Restore > Assets and select the asset to be restored and choose Restore.
    2. Select the copy of the backup to be restored. By default, the last successful backup copy is displayed. However, the copy of the backup can be selected from the list from the Change Copy option.
    3. Select the cluster to which the backup would be restored. In this case, the backup is restored to the Original Cluster.
    4. Choose the purpose. In this case, Restore Kubernetes Virtual Machines is selected which will restore the VM and its associated PVCs.
    5. Select the option of Restore to a New Namespace.
    6. Select the PVCs to be restored to the new namespace.
    7. In the Options page, choose the different VM behavior options when the restore completes.
    8. Verify the Summary and select Restore.
    9. PPDM creates a unique Job ID, and the status of the job can be viewed from the Dashboard > Jobs tab.
    10. PPDM completes the restore job in the same namespace. To verify the restore, go to the OpenShift UI and power on the VM and login to the Postgres database and verify the records.

Use case 4: Backup of container

  • Perform the steps below to deploy a PostgreSQL container on the OCP cluster in the air-gap environment:

    • On the workstation node, create an ImageSetConfiguration that includes PostgreSQL images. A sample ImageSetConfiguration file is provided below:
      apiVersion: mirror.openshift.io/v2alpha1
      kind: ImageSetConfiguration
      mirror:
        additionalImages:
          - name: registry.redhat.io/rhel9/postgresql-15:latest
          - name: registry.redhat.io/rhel9/postgresql-16:latest
    • Download the images on the workstation using oc mirror --v2 command.
    • Move the entire directory contents from workstation node to bastion node.
    • On the bastion node, push the images to the local registry using oc mirror --v2 command.
    • Create PostgreSQL Deployment Manifest on bastion node. A sample PostgreSQL YAML deployment is provided in the Sample YAML files section.
    • Deploy PostgreSQL to OpenShift Cluster by applying the manifest.
    • Verify the deployment by checking the state of PostgreSQL deployment and pods.

    To manually trigger a backup of the namespace, perform the following steps:

    1. Prior to taking a backup, the status of the Postgres database running in the container is noted. 
      [root@rb-bastion postgres]# oc exec -it -n postgres pod/postgres-7d7cc45d88-zhs78 -- bash
      bash-5.1$ psql
      psql (16.13)
      Type "help" for help.
      postgres=# select * from employees_salary ;
       employee_id | employee_name | salary
      -------------+---------------+--------
            125823 | Bob           |  95452
            125321 | John          | 116328
            125673 | Laura         | 105672
            125999 | Tim           | 110831
            125147 | Josh          | 112021
            125438 | Charles       | 114239
            125501 | Klara         | 113609
            125688 | Rose          | 112351
      (8 rows)
    2. Go to Dashboard > Protection > Protection Policies. Select the protection policy and click on Protect Now.
    3. PPDM creates a unique job ID and can be seen from Dashboard > Jobs tab.
    4. The status of the job can be observed by clicking on the Job Group ID and then looking at the step log tab.
    5. After the backup is completed, few more records are added into the Postgres database. 
      postgres=# select * from employees_salary ;
       employee_id | employee_name | salary
      -------------+---------------+--------
            125823 | Bob           |  95452
            125321 | John          | 116328
            125673 | Laura         | 105672
            125999 | Tim           | 110831
            125147 | Josh          | 112021
            125438 | Charles       | 114239
            125501 | Klara         | 113609
            125688 | Rose          | 112351
            125763 | Liam          | 103562
            125985 | Kim           | 115643
            125166 | Joe           | 232021
      (11 rows)

      postgres=#

Use case 5: Restore of container to new namespace

  • To restore the container in the new namespace, follow the steps below:

    1. Go to Dashboard > Restore > Assets and select the asset to be restored and choose Restore.
    2. Select the copy of the backup to be restored. By default, the last successful backup copy is displayed. However, the copy of the backup can be selected from the list from Change Copy option.
    3. Select the cluster to which the backup would be restored. In this case, backup is restored to the original cluster.
    4. Choose the purpose. In this case, Restore Namespace and Select PVCs should be selected, which will restore the container and its associated PVCs.
    5. In this case, Restore to New Namespace option is selected.
    6. Select whether the PVCs content needs to be overwritten or skip restore of existing PVC. If required, the PVCs and VMs can be excluded as well.
    7. If required, enable the Troubleshooting mode in the Options page.
    8. Verify the Summary and select Restore.
    9. PPDM creates a unique Job ID, and the status of the job can be viewed from Dashboard > Jobs tab.
    10. The restore job is completed in the new namespace. To verify the restore, login to the postgres pod in the new namespace and then login to Postgres database and verify the records. 
      [root@rb-bastion postgres]# oc exec -it -n postgres-restore pod/postgres-58f49c8d-zx6m8 -- bash
      bash-5.1$ psql
      psql (16.13)
      Type "help" for help.

      postgres=# select * from employees_salary ;
       employee_id | employee_name | salary
      -------------+---------------+--------
            125823 | Bob           |  95452
            125321 | John          | 116328
            125673 | Laura         | 105672
            125999 | Tim           | 110831
            125147 | Josh          | 112021
            125438 | Charles       | 114239
            125501 | Klara         | 113609
            125688 | Rose          | 112351
      (8 rows)

      postgres=#

      The Postgres database is successfully restored to the state when the backup was taken.
